title: A Study of Tersolisib (LY4064809) in Participants With Liver Impairment Compared With Participants With Normal Liver Impairment.
official: A Phase 1, Multicenter, Open-Label, Nonrandomized, Parallel-Design, Single-Dose Study to Assess the Pharmacokinetics and Safety of Tersolisib in Participants With Hepatic Impairment Compared With Participants With Normal Hepatic Function
summary:
The main purpose of this study is to measure how much tersolisib gets into the bloodstream and how long it takes the body to eliminate it in participants with liver impairment compared to participants with normal liver function. The safety of tersolisib will also be evaluated.

For each participant, the study will last about 7 weeks including a 14-night stay in the Clinical Research Unit (CRU) and one follow-up telephone call.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Have a body mass index (BMI) within the range 18 to 40 kilograms per square meter (kg/m²), inclusive.
* Participants assigned male at birth (AMAB) who agree to follow contraception guidance or participants assigned female at birth (AFAB) who are individuals not of childbearing potential (INOCBP) .

Participants with Normal Hepatic Function:

* Are healthy with normal hepatic function
* Have normal blood pressure and pulse rate.

Participants with Hepatic Impairment:

* Have mild, moderate or severe hepatic impairment classified as Child-Pugh score A, B, or C.
* Participants must have a diagnosis of chronic hepatic impairment of greater than 6 months with no clinically significant changes.
* Have acceptable blood pressure as defined by systolic blood pressure less than 160 millimeters of mercury (mmHg) and diastolic blood pressure less than 95 mmHg, as well as an acceptable pulse rate as defined by no less than 50 beats per minute (bpm) and no greater than 100 bpm.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Have a history or presence of any of the following clinically significant conditions: metabolic, biliary, gastrointestinal, hematological, neurological diseases, active cardiovascular (CV) disease or history of myocardial infarction within 3 months of planned dose of tersolisib, and a 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) abnormality that is clinically significant at screening.
* Have a clinically significant history of multiple or severe drug hypersensitivity reactions, or drug allergies, such as anaphylaxis, hepatotoxicity, or treatment with steroids or epinephrine.
* Have a history of a major surgical procedure within 30 days prior to screening.
* Have been diagnosed with, or treated for, malignancy within 5 years prior to screening with the exception of curatively treated basal cell carcinoma of the skin, squamous cell carcinoma of the skin, and curatively resected in situ carcinoma of the cervix.
* Have active uncontrolled systemic bacterial, viral, fungal or parasitic infection.
* Have evidence of Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) infection or positive HIV-1 and HIV-2 antibodies.
* Have a current infection with Hepatitis C Virus (HCV), that is, positive for HCV Ribonucleic Acid (RNA).
* Have a current infection with Hepatitis B Virus (HBV), that is, positive test for Hepatitis B Surface Antigen (HBsAg) or polymerase chain reaction positive for HBV DNA.

Participants with Normal Hepatic Function:

* Have a significant history of or presence of hepatic disease, including abnormal Liver Function Tests, as defined by aspartate aminotransferase (AST), alanine aminotransferase (ALT), or total bilirubin (TBL) above 1.5 times upper limit normal (1.5 × ULN) per the laboratory's reference ranges at screening.

Participants with Hepatic Impairment:

* Have had variceal bleeding within 3 months of check-in, unless the participant has undergone a successful banding procedure in which case they may check-in from 1 month after the banding procedure.
* Have a presence of an active portal shunt or transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt, or a medical history of a portal systemic shunt or transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt.
* Have a history of liver transplantation.
* Have a recent history of paracentesis, that is within 30 days prior to screening.
* Show presence of hepatocellular carcinoma.
* Have required new medication for hepatic encephalopathy within the 1 month prior to admission.
* Have evidence of spontaneous bacterial peritonitis within 6 months of screening.
